 Valve responds to Steam devs getting extortion emails threatening AI clones of their games
 Valve told indie devs at Steam Indie Connect that it won't gatekeep AI tools, and asked devs hit by AI clone extortion emails to officially report them.
 VIEW GALLERY - 2 Steam is at the center of developers' concerns about AI-generated game clones and extortion threats. Jak Connor Tech and Science Editor Published Oct 28, 2026 5:07 AM CDT 1-minute read time What you need to know
 Valve announced no new AI rules and said it won't dictate which tools developers use. It urged indie developers facing threats to clone their games unless they pay to report the cases to Steam, so Valve can investigate and help.

Valve has responded to indie developers worried about AI slop and AI cloned games flooding Steam, with the company saying it won't act as a gatekeeper on which tools developers use, but it does want to hear about developers being threatened with AI clones of their games.
 2 Valve asked developers to report AI clone extortion threats through official channels, but announced no new policy on AI tools. VIEW GALLERY - 2 IMAGES The comments come from Inven Global's report on Steam Indie Connect, a developer event held in Busan, South Korea, on October 27, where Valve's Steam Business Team members Tom Giardino and Marc Wilkinson took questions from developers. One indie developer said studios have been receiving extortion emails that read, " If you don't pay, we'll clone your game with AI and release it first, " and asked whether Steam has any plans to implement protections for developers.
 It was only recently that I reported on an indie game developer receiving an extortion email demanding $200 in Steam items within 24 hours for them not to release a clone of the developer's game. Giardino said it was the first he had heard of such cases, called them a matter for law enforcement, and added, " If you report such cases to us, we want to look into them further and help in whatever way we can. "

 Read more : Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney can't stop going after Steam, calls its AI disclosure policy 'abhorrent' 
 So, is Valve changing its rules on AI? No new policy was announced. Giardino said, " We don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use, " and explained that clones were around long before AI, with developers spotting an interesting concept during Steam Next Fest and quickly making a similar game.
 Story Q&A
 Powered by TweakBot
 From TweakTown's coverage of this story.
 How can indie developers officially report AI-clone extortion threats to Valve?
 Valve asked developers who receive AI-clone extortion threats to report the cases to the company so it can investigate and help where it can. It did not specify a reporting form, email address, or other official submission method; Tom Giardino also said the threats are a matter for law enforcement. How does Steam's AI disclosure policy cover content generated live during gameplay?
 Steam requires disclosure for AI-generated content in shipped games, according to the separate story "Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney can't stop going after Steam, calls its AI disclosure policy 'abhorrent'." That story does not specify how the requirement applies to content generated live during gameplay. Valve announced no new AI policy at Steam Indie Connect. How does Valve handle reports that a Steam game copies another developer's work?
 Valve asks developers who receive threats to clone their games to report them so it can look into the cases and help where it can. It called the extortion threats a matter for law enforcement, but did not specify how it handles reports about Steam games that have already copied another developer's work. Has Valve changed Steam's AI rules since the Steam Indie Connect comments?
 No new AI policy was announced at Steam Indie Connect. The separate story "Valve changes AI disclosure guidelines, 'AI powered tools' are now exempt" reports a change to Steam's disclosure rules, but it does not establish whether that change happened after those comments. However, AI-powered development tools have certainly sped up the time it takes for a clone to reach a viable state and threaten the original. A prime example is all of the PlayStation games unofficially making their way over to PC, not to mention being playable within other games such as Roblox.
